_national.varieties: Each Anbaugebiet specification lists its permitted varieties (dozens, including PIWI crosses). A single named variety needs 85% (EU); two or more named varieties must make up 100%, in descending order. Deutscher Wein (no GI) may not name 19 classic varieties incl. Riesling, Spätburgunder, Silvaner, Müller-Thurgau, Grauer and Weißer Burgunder, Dornfelder, Lemberger, Trollinger.
_national.min_alcohol: Natural minimums are set per Anbaugebiet and variety in each PDO spec within federal floors: Zone A (12 regions) Qualitätswein at least 7.0% potential (Ahr, Mittelrhein, Mosel, Saale-Unstrut may go to 6.0% for some varieties/sites), Prädikatswein at least 9.5% (9.0%); Zone B (Baden) 8.0% and 10.0%. Eiswein must reach at least the region's Beerenauslese minimum. Actual alcohol: QbA, Kabinett, Spätlese, Auslese at least 7% vol; BA, TBA, Eiswein at least 5.5% vol. Landwein (PGI) natural minimum 6.0% (Zone A), 6.5% (Zone B).
_national.max_yield: Set per Anbaugebiet by the Länder/specs (Ahr 100, Mosel 125, Pfalz/Rheinhessen/Nahe/Mittelrhein 105, Baden 90, Franken 90, Württemberg 110 hl/ha). Overproduction up to 20% may be carried forward (Übermenge); beyond that it must be distilled.
_national.ageing: No national ageing minimums for still wine. Sekt b.A.: EU minimum 9 months production for bottle fermentation (6 for tank), at least 90 days on lees. VDP.Sekt (private): traditional method, hand-picked estate grapes, whole-bunch pressing, at least 15 months on lees (24 for vintage); VDP.Sekt.Prestige at least 36 months. Barrique/wood terms need at least 75% of the wine in wood for at least 6 months (red) or 4 months (other); "Barrique" casks max 350 L.
_national.release: Ortswein (commune name): not to consumers before 15 December of the harvest year. Lagenwein (Einzellage/Gewann): not before 1 March of the following year. Großes Gewächs (pre-Sept-2026 rules): whites from 1 September after harvest, reds from 1 June of the second year; Erstes Gewächs from 1 March.
_national.styles: Deutscher Wein (wine without GI); Landwein (PGI, 26 Landweingebiete, 85% origin, no cold concentration, sweetening only with domestic must); Qualitätswein (PDO, enrichment allowed, official A.P. test number); Prädikatswein (no enrichment, sweetening only with grape must): Kabinett, Spätlese (fully ripe, late harvest), Auslese (fully ripe or botrytised), Beerenauslese (botrytised or at least overripe berries), Trockenbeerenauslese (largely shrivelled botrytised berries), Eiswein (grapes frozen at harvest and pressing). Sekt b.A., Winzersekt, Qualitätsperlwein b.A., Qualitätslikörwein b.A.
_national.labelling: 2021 origin pyramid (binding from the 2026 vintage): Anbaugebiet (PDO) < Region (Bereich or Großlage, prefixed "Region") < Ortswein (commune, at least Kabinett-level must weight) < Lagenwein (Einzellage or cadastral Gewann, village name on the label, varieties restricted by each spec, Kabinett-level must). "Qualitätswein" may be replaced by "geschützte Ursprungsbezeichnung" + region. A.P. number required on QbA and Prädikat wines. Bottling terms: Erzeugerabfüllung, Gutsabfüllung (trained winemaker, vineyards farmed since 1 Jan of harvest year), Schlossabfüllung (listed castle, own grapes only). Steillage = slope of at least 30%. Riesling-Hochgewächs: 100% Riesling, natural alcohol 1.5% above the minimum, A.P. score at least 3.0.
_national.sweetness: EU terms: trocken max 4 g/l, or 9 g/l if total acidity is no more than 2 g/l below the sugar; halbtrocken max 12 g/l, or 18 g/l if acidity is within 10 g/l; lieblich max 45 g/l; süß at least 45 g/l. "Feinherb" is permitted but not legally defined. Sekt: brut nature <3, extra brut 0-6, brut <12, extra trocken 12-17, trocken 17-32, halbtrocken 32-50, mild >50 g/l. Prädikat names indicate ripeness at harvest, not sweetness.
_national.other: Großes Gewächs and Erstes Gewächs: the 13th amending ordinance (Bundesrat 12 June 2026; BGBl. 2026 I Nr. 243 of 24 Aug 2026) rewrote WeinV s.30 so both become federally protected quality marks awarded by the Komitee - Klassifikation Erster und Großer Lagen in Deutschland e.V. (founded by the DWV and VDP) to PDO wines meeting its ministry-approved criteria, which must include a site classification. Until the 2030 vintage, or until those criteria take effect, the pre-September-2026 rules continue: GG single regional variety, hand-picked, max 50 hl/ha, at least 12% natural alcohol, dry, panel-tested; EG single variety, max 60 hl/ha (70 on steep slopes), at least 11%, dry. Classic and Crémant also have transitional rules to the 2028 vintage. Rosé/Weißherbst: Weißherbst = one red variety, at least 95% light-pressed must; Rotling blends of red and white grapes (Schillerwein Württemberg, Badisch Rotgold Baden, Schieler Sachsen). Liebfraumilch: white QbA from Nahe, Pfalz, Rheingau or Rheinhessen, at least 70% Riesling, Silvaner, Müller-Thurgau or Kerner, lieblich, no variety or smaller site on label. Classic: one regional variety, natural alcohol 1% over the minimum, total alcohol at least 12% (11.5% Mosel), RS max 15 g/l and max 2x acidity, vintage required, no taste term or Prädikat. Winzersekt: estate or co-op grapes, traditional method, at least 9 months on lees, variety and vintage stated. Eiswein: the law only requires grapes frozen at harvest and pressing; the DWI gives at least minus 7 C as the practical threshold. VDP (private, not law): Gutswein; Ortswein (max 75 hl/ha, release recommended from 1 March); Erste Lage (max 60 hl/ha, selective hand harvest, dry wines labelled Qualitätswein trocken, released from the end-April VDP Weinbörse); Große Lage (max 50 hl/ha, hand-picked, regional varieties; dry wines = VDP.Großes Gewächs, whites released 1 September after harvest, reds 1 September of the second year after at least 12 months in oak; sweet Prädikat wines from 1 May after harvest).
